concepts.name: Angling
concepts.definition: Rotating, raising, or lowering the pelvis during penetration to adjust where internal stimulation occurs.
concepts.summary: Angling involves making subtle adjustments to pelvic position during penetrative activity.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you ever shifted your hips during penetration to find an angle that felt better?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Angling is tilting your pelvis—forward, back, or side to side—to change where internal stimulation lands.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: How pelvic tilt redirects pressure along the anterior wall

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: In the OMGyes Pleasure Report (Hensel et al., 2021), about nine in ten women reported using angling. Research suggests that naming a movement can help you notice it in the moment and repeat what works—instead of relying on vague “that felt good last time.”

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you ever noticed yourself tilting your hips to change how something feels? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am curious about exploring angling slowly, with check-ins about what feels good and what does not.

phraseTemplates.label: Direct share
phraseTemplates.body: I am curious about exploring angling slowly, with check-ins about what feels good and what does not.

citations.label: Hensel et al., 2021, PLOS ONE
citations.note: Identified in the OMGyes Pleasure Report research as one of four named techniques associated with enhanced pleasure. The research found that having language for this movement helped women recognize and replicate what works for them.

concepts.name: Rocking
concepts.definition: A grinding or rocking motion that keeps consistent contact with external areas during penetration.
concepts.summary: Rocking refers to a grinding, circular, or back-and-forth motion during penetrative activity that maintains continuous contact between bodies - particularly at the point where external sensitive areas meet a partner's body.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you noticed that grinding or circular movements sometimes feel better than thrusting?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Rocking is a grinding or wave-like motion that keeps steady external contact during penetration—often without using your hands.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Compression and friction at the pubic mound

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Studies suggest most women need clitoral stimulation for orgasm; penetration alone often provides limited external contact. Rocking keeps bodies close so pressure on the clitoral area can stay continuous rather than breaking with each thrust (Hensel et al., 2021).

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you noticed a difference between grinding/rocking motions versus thrusting? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am curious about exploring rocking slowly, with check-ins about what feels good and what does not.

phraseTemplates.label: Direct share
phraseTemplates.body: I am curious about exploring rocking slowly, with check-ins about what feels good and what does not.

citations.label: Hensel et al., 2021, PLOS ONE
citations.note: Research shows that consistent external stimulation is important for pleasure for many women. Rocking was identified as a specific named technique that facilitates this during partnered penetrative activity.

concepts.name: Shallowing
concepts.definition: Focusing stimulation at or just inside the vaginal entrance rather than deeper penetration.
concepts.summary: Shallowing describes pleasurable touch that focuses on the vaginal entrance and the area just inside - using fingertips, tongue, or the tip of a toy or partner rather than deeper penetration.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you noticed that the first moments of penetration—right at the entrance—can feel especially sensitive?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Shallowing is focusing touch at the vaginal entrance and the first inch or two inside—not treating depth as the goal.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Nerve-rich tissue at the introitus

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: The introitus is densely innervated. In Hensel et al. (2021), shallowing was widely reported, and many participants said lingering at the entrance made later touch feel better—consistent with anatomy, not “just teasing.”

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you noticed that the entrance area can feel especially sensitive? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am curious about exploring shallowing slowly, with check-ins about what feels good and what does not.

phraseTemplates.label: Direct share
phraseTemplates.body: I am curious about exploring shallowing slowly, with check-ins about what feels good and what does not.

citations.label: Hensel et al., 2021, PLOS ONE
citations.note: The vaginal entrance (introitus) contains a high density of nerve endings. Research identified shallowing as a distinct technique that many women find pleasurable, challenging assumptions that deeper always means better.

concepts.name: Pairing
concepts.definition: Adding external clitoral stimulation during penetration, either solo or with a partner.
concepts.summary: Pairing means combining internal penetration with external clitoral stimulation - using your own hand, a partner's hand, a toy, or body positioning to add external touch during penetrative activity.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you found that penetration alone doesn't quite get you there—but adding clitoral touch changes everything?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Pairing is combining penetration with clitoral stimulation—your hand, a partner's hand, a toy, or positioning that adds external touch.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Internal and external stimulation in parallel

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Research consistently links clitoral stimulation with higher orgasm likelihood during partnered sex. Frederick et al. (2018) and the OMGyes work (Hensel et al., 2021) report that many women pair penetration with external touch—not as a fix, but as a common, physiologically sensible pattern.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Do you find that penetration feels better when combined with external touch? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am curious about exploring pairing slowly, with check-ins about what feels good and what does not.

phraseTemplates.label: Direct share
phraseTemplates.body: I am curious about exploring pairing slowly, with check-ins about what feels good and what does not.

citations.label: Hensel et al., 2021, PLOS ONE
citations.note: Extensive research shows that the clitoris, not the vagina, is the primary site of orgasmic sensation for most women. Studies find that adding clitoral stimulation during penetration significantly increases likelihood of orgasm.

concepts.name: Building
concepts.definition: A gradual increase in arousal intensity over time, like a wave gathering strength.
concepts.summary: Building describes the experience of arousal intensifying progressively - not jumping immediately to peak sensation, but allowing pleasure to accumulate and deepen over time.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you felt arousal start small—a hint of warmth, a whisper of tingling—then slowly intensify into something unmistakable?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Building is arousal that gathers gradually—warmth and intensity increasing over time rather than arriving all at once.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Vascular and neural intensity rising over time

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Sexual response models describe an arousal-building phase before plateau or orgasm. Research suggests that allowing sensation to accumulate—rather than rushing—is often associated with stronger peaks (Masters & Johnson; Basson, 2000).

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you noticed pleasure intensifying gradually rather than all at once? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am learning to notice building as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

phraseTemplates.label: Soft share
phraseTemplates.body: I am learning to notice building as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

citations.label: Masters & Johnson
citations.note: Research on sexual response cycles identifies arousal building as a distinct phase. Studies show that extended arousal periods often correlate with more satisfying experiences and stronger orgasms.

citations.label: Basson, 2000

concepts.name: Plateauing
concepts.definition: Sustained arousal at a consistent level without increase - a holding pattern that may precede orgasm or signal a need for change.
concepts.summary: Plateauing is the experience of arousal staying at a steady level - neither building toward climax nor fading. It's like reaching a landing on a staircase and staying there for a while.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you reached a point where arousal stays steady—not fading, but not climbing either? Like hovering at a certain altitude?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Plateauing is arousal holding steady—neither climbing toward orgasm nor fading away.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Sustained activation without a new peak

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Classic sexual response research describes a plateau phase—high arousal maintained without immediate climax (Masters & Johnson). Recognizing it helps you choose: savor the hover, or adjust stimulation if you want something to change.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you noticed arousal leveling off at a consistent intensity? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am learning to notice plateauing as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

phraseTemplates.label: Soft share
phraseTemplates.body: I am learning to notice plateauing as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

citations.label: Masters & Johnson sexual response cycle
citations.note: Sexual response research identifies a plateau phase as common in arousal cycles. Understanding this phase helps differentiate between a natural pause and a signal that stimulation needs adjustment.

concepts.name: Edging
concepts.definition: Intentionally approaching the edge of orgasm, then easing back before it happens - often repeated multiple times.
concepts.summary: Edging is the practice of bringing yourself (or being brought) close to orgasm, then deliberately pausing or slowing to pull back from the edge.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you ever gotten close to orgasm, pulled back, then approached again—and noticed the eventual release felt more intense?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Edging is deliberately approaching orgasm, then easing back before you cross—often repeating the cycle.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Intensity rising toward a threshold, then receding

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Research on orgasm delay suggests that prolonged arousal before release is often subjectively more intense for some people. Edging can also sharpen awareness of your own pre-orgasm signals—when to slow, pause, or change rhythm.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you ever intentionally paused right before orgasm to prolong the experience? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am learning to notice edging as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

phraseTemplates.label: Soft share
phraseTemplates.body: I am learning to notice edging as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

citations.label: Research on orgasm delay and intensity
citations.source: Research on orgasm delay and intensity
citations.note: Studies on orgasm intensity suggest that delayed orgasm following extended arousal often feels more powerful. Edging is also studied as a technique for orgasm control and sexual mindfulness.

concepts.name: Spreading
concepts.definition: The sensation of arousal radiating outward from its origin point through the body.
concepts.summary: Spreading describes how pleasure can expand beyond the area being stimulated - radiating outward like ripples in water.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you felt pleasure radiate outward from where you're being touched—warmth or tingling traveling through your body like ripples in water?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Spreading is arousal radiating outward from where you're touched—into the pelvis, spine, limbs, or whole body.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Neural signals propagating beyond the contact point

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Embodied sexuality research links attention to whole-body sensation with more satisfying sexual experiences. Spreading is one pattern people report when arousal feels less “localized” and more distributed.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you noticed pleasure traveling from one area through other parts of your body? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am learning to notice spreading as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

phraseTemplates.body: I am learning to notice spreading as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

concepts.name: Pulsing
concepts.definition: Rhythmic, wave-like sensations during high arousal or orgasm - a beating or throbbing quality.
concepts.summary: Pulsing refers to the rhythmic quality that pleasure can take on - a beating, throbbing, or wave-like pattern.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you noticed a rhythmic, throbbing quality during high arousal or orgasm—like waves of sensation beating through you?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Pulsing is a rhythmic, throbbing quality in arousal or orgasm—waves of sensation rather than a flat steady tone.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Concentric contraction waves in pelvic floor tissue

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Physiology studies describe rhythmic pelvic muscle contractions during orgasm, often about once per second (Meston & Buss, 2009). Many people also notice pulse-like sensation earlier in arousal—and some prefer stimulation that matches or contrasts that rhythm.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you noticed a rhythmic, beating quality to arousal or orgasm? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am learning to notice pulsing as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

phraseTemplates.body: I am learning to notice pulsing as useful information about my pleasure, not something I need to force.

concepts.name: Warm-up Window
concepts.definition: The time needed for whole-body arousal before genital-focused stimulation feels best - often 20+ minutes.
concepts.summary: The warm-up window refers to the period of time many bodies need for full arousal before genital-focused stimulation becomes most pleasurable.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you noticed that touch feels better after you've had time to warm up—and that rushing makes everything feel less enjoyable?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: The warm-up window is how long many bodies need for full arousal before genital-focused touch feels best—often twenty minutes or more of whole-body stimulation.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Engorgement and blood flow increasing over time

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Genital blood flow, lubrication, and subjective arousal often rise gradually (Chivers et al., 2010). Adequate warm-up is associated in research with greater comfort and reported pleasure—not a personal failing, but common physiology.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Do you find that touch feels better after you've had time to get warmed up? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: My timing may follow warm-up window; I would like room for that pace instead of treating it as a problem.

phraseTemplates.label: Reassuring share
phraseTemplates.body: My timing may follow warm-up window; I would like room for that pace instead of treating it as a problem.

citations.note: Studies on genital blood flow and arousal timing show significant gender differences. Research indicates that adequate warm-up time correlates with better lubrication, comfort, and reported pleasure.

concepts.name: Responsive Desire
concepts.definition: Sexual interest that arises in response to stimulation or erotic context, rather than appearing spontaneously beforehand.
concepts.summary: Responsive desire describes a pattern where sexual interest emerges in response to something - a partner's initiation, an erotic situation, or physical stimulation that's already begun - rather than arising spontaneously as an internal urge.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Do you rarely feel random urges for sex—but once things start, you get into it and enjoy yourself fully?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Responsive desire is interest that shows up after stimulation, context, or connection—not as a spontaneous urge beforehand.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: A spark of context, then desire blooming

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Desire research (Basson, 2000; Nagoski, 2015) describes responsive desire as a common, healthy pattern—especially for women and in long-term relationships. Lack of spontaneous urge beforehand does not mean low libido; many people become interested once touch or mood engages them.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Do you rarely feel spontaneous urges for sex, but enjoy it once you get started? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: My timing may follow responsive desire; I would like room for that pace instead of treating it as a problem.

phraseTemplates.label: Reassuring share
phraseTemplates.body: My timing may follow responsive desire; I would like room for that pace instead of treating it as a problem.

citations.label: Nagoski, 2015
citations.note: Dr. Emily Nagoski's synthesis of desire research highlights responsive desire as a normal, common pattern. Studies show responsive desire is particularly common for women and doesn't indicate low libido.

concepts.name: Spontaneous Desire
concepts.definition: Sexual interest that arises on its own, without an external trigger - a seemingly random urge for sexual activity.
concepts.summary: Spontaneous desire is sexual interest that appears to come from nowhere - an internal urge or wanting that arises without an obvious external stimulus.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Do you sometimes feel sexually interested out of nowhere—an urge that appears without any obvious cause?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Spontaneous desire is interest that appears on its own—often described as “being in the mood” without an obvious trigger.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Internal arousal signals rising independently

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Population studies suggest spontaneous desire is reported more often by men than women, and more often early in relationships (Basson, 2000). It is one valid pattern—not the only one. Many people experience a mix of spontaneous and responsive desire over time.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Do you sometimes feel sexually interested without any obvious cause? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: My timing may follow spontaneous desire; I would like room for that pace instead of treating it as a problem.

phraseTemplates.label: Reassuring share
phraseTemplates.body: My timing may follow spontaneous desire; I would like room for that pace instead of treating it as a problem.

citations.label: Basson, 2000
citations.note: Research distinguishes between spontaneous and responsive desire patterns. Studies show that spontaneous desire is more common in men but occurs in all genders, and often decreases in frequency during long-term relationships.

concepts.name: Golden Trio
concepts.definition: Combining intercourse with manual and oral stimulation - a combination associated with 86% orgasm rates in research.
concepts.summary: The Golden Trio refers to a specific combination of activities that research has found particularly effective for women's orgasms: vaginal intercourse combined with manual stimulation combined with oral sex (in the same session, not necessarily simultaneously).

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you noticed that combining different kinds of stimulation—not just penetration—leads to more intense experiences?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: The golden trio is vaginal intercourse plus manual and oral stimulation in the same encounter—a combination linked in research to higher reported orgasm rates.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Three stimulation types in one session

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Frederick et al. (2018) found that women who received intercourse, manual genital stimulation, and oral sex in the same encounter reported orgasm more often than with intercourse alone. The takeaway is statistical, not prescriptive: variety and clitoral involvement are common in high-satisfaction reports.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you noticed that combining different types of touch leads to different experiences? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: My timing may follow golden trio; I would like room for that pace instead of treating it as a problem.

citations.note: Frederick et al. (2018) found that women who received genital stimulation, oral sex, and deep kissing in addition to vaginal intercourse reported the highest rates of orgasm during partnered sex.

concepts.name: Spectatoring
concepts.definition: Mentally watching and evaluating yourself during sex rather than staying present in the experience.
concepts.summary: Spectatoring is the experience of mentally stepping outside yourself during sex to observe and judge what's happening - focusing on how you look, whether you're responding "correctly," how long it's taking, or what your partner might be thinking.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you ever caught yourself watching yourself during sex—thinking about how you look, whether you're taking too long, or what your partner might be thinking?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Spectatoring is watching and evaluating yourself during sex instead of staying with sensation—performance thoughts replacing presence.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Attention split between body and inner critic

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Masters and Johnson named spectatoring as a barrier to enjoyment; later work links self-focused attention during sex with lower arousal and satisfaction (Barlow, 1986). Mindfulness-based approaches often help redirect attention back to sensation (Brotto, 2018).

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Do you sometimes find yourself watching yourself during sex as if from the outside? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am noticing how spectatoring affects my pleasure, and it helps when we make the experience calmer and less performative.

concepts.name: Embodied Presence
concepts.definition: Focused attention on bodily sensations during intimacy - being fully in your body rather than in your head.
concepts.summary: Embodied presence is the opposite of spectatoring - it's being fully in your body and present to sensations rather than caught up in thoughts, judgments, or mental chatter.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you experienced moments of being so absorbed in physical sensation that thinking temporarily faded—fully in your body rather than your head?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Embodied presence is staying with bodily sensation during intimacy—attention in the body rather than in commentary or judgment.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Attention filling the outline of the body

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Mindfulness-based interventions for sexual concerns show improvements in arousal and satisfaction in clinical studies (Brotto, 2018). Present-moment focus on touch is a skill—when the mind wanders, you can gently return.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you experienced moments of being completely absorbed in physical sensation? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am noticing how embodied presence affects my pleasure, and it helps when we make the experience calmer and less performative.

concepts.name: Non-concordance
concepts.definition: When physical arousal signs (lubrication, erection) don't match the subjective feeling of being turned on - and vice versa.
concepts.summary: Non-concordance is the disconnect that can occur between physical arousal signals and how turned on you actually feel.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you ever felt mentally aroused while your body showed no physical signs—or noticed physical wetness when you weren't actually interested?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Non-concordance is a mismatch between physical arousal signs (like lubrication) and how interested or turned on you actually feel.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Separate pathways for genital response and felt desire

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Meta-analyses find only modest correlation between genital response and subjective arousal in women—often cited around 10–30% overlap (Chivers et al., 2010; Nagoski, 2015). Genital response can occur without desire; desire can exist without obvious physical signs. Consent and wanting are communicated, not inferred from wetness or erection.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you ever felt turned on without your body showing typical signs of arousal? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am noticing how non-concordance affects my pleasure, and it helps when we make the experience calmer and less performative.

concepts.name: Sexual Self-Esteem
concepts.definition: A positive self-concept around sexuality - feeling good about yourself as a sexual person.
concepts.summary: Sexual self-esteem is how you feel about yourself as a sexual being - whether you view your sexuality positively, feel confident in your desirability, and have a healthy relationship with your own sexual self.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: How do you feel about yourself as a sexual person? Do you carry confidence into intimate experiences—or do negative beliefs hold you back?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Sexual self-esteem is how positively you see yourself as a sexual person—including confidence, worthiness of pleasure, and comfort with your sexuality.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Warm core sense of sexual confidence

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Research links sexual self-esteem with satisfaction, communication, and sexual function. Valuing your own pleasure and feeling entitled to it—not perfect confidence every day—is associated in studies with better outcomes over time.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: How do you generally feel about yourself as a sexual person? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.title: A Phrase To Keep
blocks.body: I am noticing how sexual self-esteem affects my pleasure, and it helps when we make the experience calmer and less performative.

concepts.name: Body Appreciation
concepts.definition: Valuing your body for what it does and feels rather than evaluating its appearance.
concepts.summary: Body appreciation is the practice of relating to your body based on sensation, function, and experience rather than visual evaluation.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: During sex, are you more focused on how your body looks—or how it feels? Do appearance concerns pull you out of sensation?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Body appreciation is valuing your body for sensation and capacity—not mainly for how it looks in the moment.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Touch activating sensory response, not visual critique

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Body image research links appreciating body function during sex with greater satisfaction and less appearance distraction (Satinsky et al., 2012). Weight alone does not predict sexual function; how you relate to your body in the moment often matters more.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: During sex, are you more focused on how your body looks or how it feels? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

blocks.body: I am noticing how body appreciation affects my pleasure, and it helps when we make the experience calmer and less performative.

concepts.name: Clitoral Structure
concepts.definition: The full clitoral organ is approximately 9cm in size, with internal legs (crura) and bulbs extending inside the body.
concepts.summary: The clitoris is much larger than it appears from the outside.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Did you know that what you can see of the clitoris is just the tip? The full structure extends about 9cm inside your body.

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: The clitoris is mostly internal: glans, shaft, crura (“legs”), and vestibular bulbs—about 9 cm total, not just the visible tip.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Crura and bulbs wrapping the vaginal canal

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: MRI and dissection work mapped the full clitoral structure (O'Connell et al., 2005). Anterior vaginal sensitivity often reflects internal clitoral and urethral tissue—not a separate “spot.” Most vaginal pleasure is still clitoral stimulation, accessed indirectly.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Did you know the clitoris extends internally beyond what's visible? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

concepts.name: Nerve Density
concepts.definition: The clitoral glans contains over 8,000 nerve endings - approximately equal to the entire penis.
concepts.summary: The clitoral glans (the visible external portion) contains more than 8,000 nerve endings - a remarkable concentration in a structure much smaller than the penis, which has approximately the same number spread across a larger area.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you noticed how incredibly sensitive the clitoral area can be—how subtle differences in pressure or touch create dramatically different sensations?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Nerve density describes how packed with nerve endings the clitoral glans is—roughly 8,000 in a small area, comparable to the penis but more concentrated.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Dense neural network in the glans

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Anatomical studies count thousands of nerve endings in the clitoral glans (O'Connell et al.). That density helps explain why touch quality—pressure, rhythm, indirect vs direct—matters so much, and why intensity can feel “too much” for some people at the wrong moment.

blocks.title: Field Note
blocks.body: Have you noticed how sensitive the clitoral area is to different types of touch? What would you want to remember about your own experience?

concepts.name: CUV Complex
concepts.definition: The integrated tissue cluster where clitoris, urethra, and anterior vaginal wall interact - explaining "G-spot" sensitivity.
concepts.summary: The clitourethrovaginal (CUV) complex describes how the clitoris, urethra, and front vaginal wall are interconnected rather than separate structures.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you experienced sensitivity on the front wall of the vagina—an area that feels different from the rest?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: The CUV complex (clitourethrovaginal) is the integrated cluster of clitoris, urethra, and anterior vaginal wall—often discussed as the “G-spot” area.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Shared tissue and pressure between three structures

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Imaging studies show these structures are physically connected, not isolated (Jannini et al., 2014). Front-wall sensitivity is real because pressure there compresses internal clitoral and urethral tissue—there is no separate magic organ to hunt for.

concepts.name: Internal Clitoral Stimulation
concepts.definition: Stimulating internal clitoral tissue through the vaginal wall - what's often called "G-spot" sensation.
concepts.summary: Internal clitoral stimulation refers to reaching the internal portions of the clitoris through the vaginal wall.

blocks.title: Recognize
blocks.body: Have you noticed that certain angles or positions create pleasurable sensations on the front wall of the vagina—different from deeper penetration?

blocks.title: Name
blocks.body: Internal clitoral stimulation is reaching clitoral tissue through the vaginal wall—especially the anterior (front) wall toward the belly button.

blocks.title: See It
blocks.body: Pressure on the anterior wall engaging internal crura

blocks.title: Understand
blocks.body: Research suggests many “vaginal” orgasms involve internal clitoral stimulation (Foldes & Buisson, 2009). Techniques like angling can improve contact with the anterior wall where crura and urethral sponge lie close to the surface.
